CS 2223.name: Algorithms
CS 2223.description: Develops algorithm design and analysis through greedy, recursive, dynamic, heuristic and probabilistic methods, using sorting, graphs and string problems.

review.rationale: Algorithm design and worst/average-case analysis establish foundational computer science.

MA 2611.name: Applied Statistics I
MA 2611.description: Introduces applied statistical analysis through study design, data exploration, estimation and hypothesis tests using real datasets and software.

review.rationale: Statistical inference and study design are the central methods, despite practical industrial/scientific examples.

MA 2612.name: Applied Statistics II
MA 2612.description: Continues applied statistics with regression, categorical-data tables, experimental analysis and distribution-free methods.

review.rationale: The complete description develops statistical methods rather than an unspecified data-science survey.

DS 1010.name: Data Science I: Introduction to Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
DS 1010.description: Introduces data preparation, programming, statistics, learning methods, visualization and responsible AI through projects with real datasets.

review.rationale: The broad introduction deliberately spans programming, mathematical analysis and AI methods without establishing one dominant subject.

DS 2010.name: Data Science II: Statistical Modeling and Analysis
DS 2010.recommended_background: Data science basics equivalent to DS 1010 , applied statistics and regression equivalent to MA 2611 and MA 2612 , and the ability to write computer programs in a scientific language equivalent to a CS programming course at the CS 1000 or CS 2000 level are assumed.
DS 2010.description: Develops prediction and inference workflows with regression, classification, decision trees, dimensionality reduction, feature engineering and bias-variance analysis.

review.rationale: After a brief mathematics review, the description explicitly centers introductory machine-learning methods and predictive data workflows.

DS 3010.name: Data Science III: Computational Methods
DS 3010.recommended_background: Data science basics equivalent to DS 1010 , and data analysis principles and modeling equivalent to DS 2010 , knowledge of basic statistics equivalent to ( MA 2611 and MA 2612 ), and the ability to program equivalent to ( CS 1004 or CS 1101 or CS 1102 ) and ( CS 2102 , CS 2103 or CS 2119 ), as well as understanding of databases equivalent to ( CS 3431 or MIS 3720 ) are assumed.
DS 3010.description: Develops large-data workflows spanning API collection, data management, cloud infrastructure and machine/deep-learning toolkits.

review.rationale: The stated pipeline combines data infrastructure and AI toolkits without a dominant single subject; it is not mathematics merely from the older title-only candidate list.

FIN 2070.name: Risk Analysis for Decision Making
FIN 2070.description: Introduces financial decisions through valuation, interest rates, investment risk and returns, establishing financial literacy for further study.

review.rationale: The actual description concerns substantive finance and valuation, not generic decision-theory mathematics or AI.
